_about: HELD-OUT set (D-184): apps chosen and ground truth written on 2026-10-26 from the repos at the pinned commits, BEFORE the analyzer was run on any of them. No analyzer rule is changed because of these results; they measure how the v1 rules generalize. Mixed languages on purpose (Rust has no rules yet). Same schema as apps.json. DRAFT until 이진서 reviews (reviewed_by null).

apps.why: HTML presentation framework; ships index.html + a vite build

evidence.finding: no runtime dependencies; vite build scripts

apps.why: note-taking server (Go) that serves its React UI; SQLite on a volume by default

evidence.finding: driver default sqlite (mysql/postgres optional); port flag 8081 bound to env with prefix MEMOS_
uploads are chunked at 2 MiB, 4 MiB per request -> not a large payload
gorilla/websocket only as an indirect dependency

apps.notes: Needs a persistent volume for SQLite and attachments (no EFS in the platform).

apps.why: web IRC client: socket.io to the browser, long-lived IRC connections, users and logs on local disk

evidence.finding: port 9000 in a config file (no PORT env); fileUpload.enable false by default

apps.notes: Port comes from config.js in THELOUNGE_HOME, not an env var: the app contract needs a config file. Users and logs need a persistent home directory.

apps.why: the original Python httpbin: stateless API, but the image pins port 80 in its CMD

evidence.finding: CMD gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:80 (command-line bind wins over GUNICORN_CMD_ARGS)

apps.notes: Same gap as hashicorp/http-echo, but through a Dockerfile CMD rather than a Go flag.

apps.why: Bitwarden-compatible server in Rust: WebSocket notifications, SQLite on /data

evidence.finding: diesel with sqlite / mysql / postgresql features

apps.notes: Rust: the v1 analyzer has no Rust rules, so this measures what it does with an unknown language.
